claims.paper: rewrite (brief Phase 5): what the ODD protocol requires
claims.claim: The 2010 update keeps seven elements but renames two and changes the design concepts
claims.source_value: 1 Purpose; 2 Entities, state variables, and scales; 3 Process overview and scheduling; 4 Design concepts (eleven: Basic principles, Emergence, Adaptation, Objectives, Learning, Prediction, Sensing, Interaction, Stochasticity, Collectives, Observation); 5 Initialization; 6 Input data; 7 Submodels. Fitness was renamed Objectives; Basic principles and Learning were added
claims.location: preprint p. 18, Table 1 (journal page not mapped); p. 9, §3 element 4
claims.quote: two elements was modified (elements 2 and 6), one design concept was renamed
claims.conditions: superseded in element 1 by the 2020 update ('Purpose and patterns'; NEW_Grimm_etal_2020)
claims.note: Table 1 read in the raw text, which keeps the two columns in order; the layout text interleaves them.

claims.paper: rewrite (brief Phase 5): which ODD version to cite
claims.claim: The 2010 update replaces the 2006 description of the elements
claims.source_value: as claimed: the updated protocol 'fully replaces' the 2006 description, which is obsolete because of its ambiguities; the 2006 account of ODD's overall purpose and rationale stays valid
claims.quote: fully replaces the original description given by Grimm et al. (2006), which is obsolete

claims.paper: rewrite (brief Phase 5): what the ODD protocol requires
claims.claim: Using ODD means using its element names in the prescribed order
claims.source_value: as claimed: exactly these identifiers in the specified order; numbering 1-7 optional; changing the order, lumping elements, renaming or omitting elements is not following ODD
claims.quote: Using ODD means using exactly these identifiers in the order specified by the protocol

claims.paper: rewrite (suggested, not in the brief): state variables and exact restart
claims.claim: ODD's test for what counts as a state variable is what must be saved to restart the model in exactly the same state
claims.source_value: as claimed: one way to define entities and state variables is to ask what must be saved so the model can be stopped and restarted later in exactly the same state; state variables must be low level (not calculable from others)
claims.quote: stop the model and save it in its current state, so it can be re-started
claims.note: This matches the project's exact-resume invariant (World.toJSON / parseSave; the resume test) and could be cited where the paper describes it.

claims.paper: rewrite (brief Phase 5): ODD for non-agent models
claims.claim: ODD can be used to document any large, complex model, not only agent-based ones
claims.quote: it can help with documenting any large, complex model

Other content the rewrite may use: the review of the 54 ODD uses to December 2009 (75 % complete or missing one element; 'Input' most often misread as parameters; preprint pp. 3-4); the design concepts are a checklist and unused ones may be left out (p. 10); Submodels should state how each submodel was designed, parameterized and tested (p. 11); pseudo-code recommended for the schedule (p. 8); limitations: ODD describes one model version, and a delta-ODD was suggested (p. 14). Quote the journal version's wording only after checking it, since this is the preprint.
